input.quote: 12.4 During the term and for twenty-four months thereafter, Customer shall not develop, market, sell, or acquire any product or service that competes with Vendor in any territory.
input.rationale: Section 12.4 binds Customer with an undefined-scope non-compete ("any product or service that competes with Vendor in any territory") running 24 months past the term — walk-away territory under this rule (post-term non-compete longer than 12 months, undefined scope) — and it contradicts the pro-Customer confirmation in Section 12.3. No other clause imposes a non-compete or field-of-use restriction on Customer (Section 13.4 is ordinary use restrictions; Section 2.2 exclusivity is a separate rule; Section 24.2 binds Vendor). We take the preferred position by striking the offending sentence as intentionally omitted, relying on the retained Section 12.3 confirmation rather than restating the same permission twice; the narrowed fallback is offered in the comment only.

ops.oldText: During the term and for twenty-four months thereafter, Customer shall not develop, market, sell, or acquire any product or service that competes with Vendor in any territory.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We cannot restrict the products or businesses we may develop, buy, or sell, so we have struck the 24-month post-term non-compete in Section 12.4 and rely on the confirmation already given in Section 12.3. If the relationship needs protection, we could discuss a restriction limited to a named competing product, during the term only, capped at 12 months, with carve-outs for our internal development and acquisitions.
proposal.summary: Strike the 24-month post-term non-compete in Section 12.4 as intentionally omitted, relying on Section 12.3.

mappings.element: Customer has no non-compete or field-of-use restriction.
